identity.identity_evidence: Read from the cartridge, not from a symbol map: extracted/overlays/overlay_0030.bin at file offset 0x0049d8 (= 0x02115b78) holds the bytes 37 64 61 4d 6b 79 5f 63 00 -- ASCII '7daMky_c' NUL-terminated, the Itanium length-prefixed _ZTS payload for a 7-character class name. _ZTI7daMky_c +4 points at exactly this address, so the string is the RTTI name of the record whose vtable the class uses.
identity.queue_name_is_not_the_rom_name: The queue row, all 9 own member symbols in config/arm9/overlays/ov030/symbols.txt, and include/Ukiki.h all spell the class 'Ukiki'. The cartridge does not. Per roles/scout.md rule 1, RTTI wins: the class is daMky_c. 'Ukiki' is a reconstruction label, not a coined-and-disclosed ROM identity.

vtable.duplicate_note: config/arm9/overlays/ov030/symbols.txt lines 143-144 declare BOTH _ZTV5Ukiki and _ZTV7daMky_c at 0x02115bfc. Two vtable symbol names for one address. Whichever name the promoted TU emits must be the one the ROM data records resolve through; see blockers.
vtable.extent_evidence: MEASURED at this revision, two independent ways that agree. (1) Bytes: the two-word ABI preamble sits at 0x02115bf4..0x02115bfb; slot 0 is at the symbol address 0x02115bfc; the last function word is slot 30 at 0x02115c74; exclusive end 0x02115c78. (2) Relocations: config/arm9/overlays/ov030/relocs.txt carries exactly 31 'kind:load' relocations at 0x02115bfc, 0x02115c00, ... 0x02115c74 (stride 4, inclusive) plus one at 0x02115bf8 for the typeinfo pointer. The two words at 0x02115c78 and 0x02115c7c are BOTH zero AND carry NO relocation, so they are not slots.
vtable.why_it_does_not_end_where_the_next_datum: The next datum is .bss at 0x02115c80, 8 bytes past the vtable's end at 0x02115c78. Those 8 zero, unrelocated bytes are section-end alignment padding: .data is declared align:32 in config/arm9/overlays/ov030/delinks.txt and 0x02115c80 is the next 32-byte boundary, while 0x02115c78 is not. mwld truncates trailing null vtable slots, so an emitted vtable never ends in nulls; combined with the absent relocations this rules out a 32- or 33-slot reading. The vtable is the last object in ov030 .data.
vtable.own_slot_test: A slot is this class's own iff its relocation names module:overlay(30); all 22 inherited slots relocate to module:main (arm9). Verified per-slot in relocs.txt.

displacement_census.what_it_is: An objective measurement, made at this revision, of every immediate-offset load/store in the 44-function run whose displacement falls in [0xd0,0x3cc). It says which offsets are LIVE. It does NOT prove the base register is `this`, and it does NOT name or type anything.
displacement_census.method: ARM immediate-offset LDR/STR/LDRB/STRB/LDRH/STRH with U=1, base register != r15.
known_blind_spots: Excluding r15 was necessary: including it added 48 spurious displacements from literal-pool reads. In particular `ldr r0,[r15,#0x3c4]` at 0x02112624 is a literal load, NOT a field access -- offsets 0x3c0..0x3c5 really are untouched.
It MISSES block transfers. The Matrix4x3 at 0x350 is written with ldm/stm and therefore does not appear in the table below at all. Absence from this table is not evidence of a dead offset.
It misses register-offset and scaled addressing.
notes: Offsets 0x0d0 through 0x184 are inside or just past the dActor_c base and the ModelAnim/ShadowModel subobjects; the base register there is frequently NOT `this`. Do not read them as own fields.

0x3bc is read exactly ONCE (at 0x021128dc, `ldr r1,[r5,#0x3bc]`) and never written with an immediate-offset store. The previous scout file's claim that it is 'incremented by 0x400 and compared with a fixed threshold' is not supported by any immediate-offset access measured here; treat its semantics as unproven.
0x3c0..0x3c5 have ZERO accesses of any measured kind.

data_and_bss.class_owns_no_data: MEASURED: not one of the 44 shards (nor either factory shard) declares a .data, .bss, .rodata or .init section in config/arm9/overlays/ov030/delinks.txt. Count of non-.text sections on class shards: 0. This is consistent with the queue's promotion_route: text-only -- and it is what makes the pointer-to-member hazard below real.

pointer_to_member_array.record_layout: { void *ptr; s32 adj; } -- the ARM Itanium pointer-to-member-function representation. In all 22 records the second word is 0 (non-virtual, zero this-adjustment) and the first word is a relocated ov030 .text address.
pointer_to_member_array.alignment_proof: The 22 relocations in relocs.txt sit at 0x02115ac8, 0x02115ad0, ... 0x02115b70 -- stride 8, starting exactly at 0x02115ac8. Reading this band 4 bytes off would pair each pointer with the wrong word and yield zero valid records; the relocation stride rules that out. The array ends exactly where _ZTS7daMky_c begins at 0x02115b78, and begins exactly where _ZTV13RollingLogTtm ends at 0x02115ac8.
pointer_to_member_array.abi_proof: func_ov030_02114170 (0x02114170) executes the textbook ARM PMF call sequence on these records: ldr r3,[r0,#0x3a4]; ldr r1,[r3,#4]; add r0,r0,r1,asr #1; ands r1,r1,#1; ldrne r2,[r0]; ldrne r1,[r3]; ldrne r1,[r2,r1]; ldreq r1,[r3]; blx r1. The `adj&1` virtual bit and the `adj>>1` this-adjustment are unmistakable. func_ov030_02114134 does the same on the record at descriptor +8.

state_descriptor_array.descriptor_layout: two consecutive 8-byte PMF records: { PMF entry; PMF tick; }
state_descriptor_array.evidence: func_ov030_021141a8 is `ldr r2,[pc,#0xc] (-> 0x02115e0c); ldr ip,[pc,#0xc] (-> 0x02114170); add r1,r2,r1,lsl #4; str r1,[r0,#0x3a4]; bx ip` -- base 0x02115e0c, index scaled by 16. 11 descriptors x 0x10 = 0xb0 = exactly the size of the 22-record .data array, and 0x02115e0c + 0xb0 = 0x02115ebc, just inside the .bss end at 0x02115ec0. The count 11 is corroborated by an 11-entry .bss pointer table at 0x02115bc8..0x02115bf4 (11 relocations, verified).
state_descriptor_array.initialised_by: __sinit_ov030_02114924 (ov030 .init, 0x02114924..0x02114dd0, size 0x4ac). Its literal pool holds 0x02115e0c at 0x02114d50 followed by all 22 PMF-record addresses at 0x02114d54..0x02114da8. Those are the only three references to 0x02115e0c / 0x02115ac8 in the whole module (relocs.txt: 0x021141bc, 0x02114d50, 0x02114d94).
state_descriptor_array.caveat: This sinit is 0x4ac bytes and also performs SharedFilePtr::Construct calls for the module's other classes, so it is a MODULE-wide initializer, not daMky_c's alone. The pairing of individual PMF records to individual descriptor indices was read from literal-pool ORDER, not from a simulated execution, and is marked unproven below.

callers.method: Two independent passes, both run at this revision.

relocation_pass.filter: Accept a relocation only when its destination module names overlay 30. dsd spells this `module:overlay(30)` (and `module:overlays(30,75)` for ambiguous ones), NEVER `ov030`; the filter parses the digits out of both spellings.
relocation_pass.phantom_ratio: 39x. 3955 of the 4059 rows that land in this address range come from 50+ OTHER overlays that share the address space (largest: overlay(22) 236, overlay(29) 200, overlay(36) 187, overlay(9) 172). Reporting them as callers would have been a 39-fold overcount.
relocation_pass.filter_sanity_check: The rejected count is 3955, i.e. non-zero, so the filter is not silently rejecting everything. Independently: config/arm9/relocs.txt DOES contain references into ov030 (5 of them -- 4 spelled `overlay(30)` and one spelled `overlays(30,75)`), so an arm9 caller would have been found had one existed.
relocation_pass.result: All 104 accepted references originate from ov030 itself. ZERO references into the class's text run come from arm9 or from any other overlay.

text_decode_pass.why: roles/scout.md warns a relocation scan can miss intra-overlay BL. In this tree every function is its own delink shard, so inter-function calls DO carry relocations -- but the decode was run anyway as an independent check.
text_decode_pass.the_two: 0x021145f0 -> 0x02114628 and 0x02114648 -> 0x02114680. Both are a factory's own internal forward `beq` (the null-check skip), i.e. intra-function branches, not calls in.
text_decode_pass.result: Agrees with the relocation pass: no ov030 code outside the 44-function run branches into it.

blockers.title: 22 pointer-to-member records in UNOWNED .data resolve their targets BY NAME
blockers.detail: The class owns no .data (measured: 0 non-.text sections across all 44 shards), so the 22-record PMF array at 0x02115ac8 stays in unowned .data while its 22 targets move into the promoted TU. dsd resolves those records by SYMBOL NAME. If any of those 22 functions is renamed from func_ov030_* to a daMky_c:: member without the matching row landing in config/arm9/overlays/ov030/symbols.txt IN THE SAME COMMIT, that record links as 0x00000000. No stage-2 or stage-3 byte gate catches it. The 22 affected addresses are listed under data_and_bss.pointer_to_member_array.targets_in_array_order.
blockers.also: A class member function cannot sit inside an `extern "C" { }` region, so the file-scope region must go after the last surviving func_* member.

blockers.title: The class name in the tree is not the class name in the ROM
blockers.detail: Every one of the 9 own member symbols is spelled _ZN5Ukiki*, and include/Ukiki.h declares `Ukiki`. The cartridge says daMky_c, proven by the _ZTS string at 0x02115b78 and confirmed by tools/rtti_vtables.py, whose canonical key is daMky_c and which does not recognise 'Ukiki' at all. Writing the class as daMky_c re-mangles all 9 member symbols (5 -> 7 characters) and changes _ZTV5Ukiki to _ZTV7daMky_c -- a coordinated rename touching symbols.txt, the header, and every shard, in one commit. Writing it as Ukiki keeps the tree consistent but ships a class name the ROM contradicts. This is a SCOPE DECISION for the writer/reviewer, not something the scout should settle; the ROM fact is recorded here either way.

blockers.title: Two _ZTV symbols at one address
blockers.detail: config/arm9/overlays/ov030/symbols.txt declares both _ZTV5Ukiki (line 143) and _ZTV7daMky_c (line 144) at 0x02115bfc. Whichever name the promoted TU emits must be the one the data records resolve through, and romdata_check is the only vtable gate. Resolve the duplicate as part of the naming decision above.

blockers.title: The TU owns all 9 virtuals, so it will want to emit the vtable
blockers.detail: All 9 own vtable targets including both out-of-line destructors are inside the 44-shard run, and an out-of-line destructor is the key function. A TU that owns every virtual emits _ZTV -- but the route is text-only and the class owns no .data. Whether the vtable ends up emitted, and in which order the destructor variants come out, is the thing most likely to cost this promotion; the destructor-position and defer_codegen levers apply. Note there is no D2 to order.

blockers.title: 20 of 44 shards are still .c
blockers.detail: Folding them into one .cpp is a language-mode flip as well as a merge, and language mode is transitive through includes.

unproven: The class name as written in the original 2004 source. The cartridge proves the RTTI identity is daMky_c and proves 'Ukiki' occurs nowhere in the ROM in any case; it does not prove what the .cpp file or the C++ identifier was called. 'Ukiki' is a prior reconstruction label carried by the tree, NOT a coined-and-disclosed name with ROM evidence behind it.

The original identifiers of all 35 non-virtual functions, and whether each was a member function or a file-local free function. What IS proven: their addresses, sizes, contiguous TU membership, inbound call counts, and which 22 of them are reached through pointer-to-member records. 22 being PMF targets is strong evidence those 22 are non-static MEMBER functions -- a PMF record can only point at one -- but it does not supply their names.

The names of every own field. The five constructor/destructor-proven subobjects, the Matrix4x3 block at 0x350, and the two dispatcher-proven words at 0x3a4 and 0x3b4 are proven as STORAGE; no field NAME in include/Ukiki.h (mSpawnPosX/Y/Z, mCapUniqueID, mCapPlayerNo, mHasSpawnedCap, unk_*) was read from the ROM.

The displacement census proves each is live and gives its access width and read/write mix; it proves nothing about semantics. contradiction_found.detail: The shard src/func_ov030_02112a14.c carried the provenance comments `recovered name: daObjHmMaruta_c_AfterClsn` and `daObjHmMaruta_c::AfterClsn - recovered from vtable slot identity`, and its body read through a `struct daObjHmMaruta_c *`. That attribution is contradicted by the ROM: 0x02112a14 is pointer-to-member record 0 of daMky_c's 22-record array at 0x02115ac8, it lies inside daMky_c's contiguous text run, and it writes the immediate 8 to daMky_c's state word. It is daMky_c's state-8 entry handler. The two classes evidently share the dActor_c field offsets the body touches, which is how the wrong header still compiled.
